calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for shot volume, and the Mammoth are one of the league’s best at keeping shots away. Our lean: the Devils’ shot volume wins out.
calls.call: The Devils take more than the league-average 56.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 against the Mammoth.
calls.nums: New Jersey 3rd for shot volume (65.0 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Utah 4th for keeping shots away
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts, New Jersey had 56.6 per 60. The league average is 56.5 per 60, and they came in at 65.0 per 60.

calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: On depth, Utah is the league’s best and New Jersey is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Mammoth spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Devils.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, Utah had 47% and New Jersey 42%. Coming in, Utah was at 44% and New Jersey at 40%.
calls.beyond: Utah’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 44% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 8 games.

NJD.head: We gave New Jersey a 63% chance, but Utah had other ideas.

UTA.head: We gave Utah a 37% chance, and Utah proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Utah’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Utah’s power play created 14.7 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.1 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: New Jersey tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Lombardi, C. Glass, J. Boqvist played 7:43 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of New Jersey’s usual lines.

story.head: The Mammoth beat the Devils
paras: Clayton Keller opened the scoring 1:57 in. Five different Mammoth scored. Twice the Devils answered a Mammoth lead. Lawson Crouse scored the winner late in the second.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. By our Swing measure, Nick Schmaltz had the best night of anyone. The Devils tried a line they hadn’t used before: Amadeus Lombardi, Cody Glass and Jesper Boqvist.

items.text: Whether the Devils keep that line together at home against Vancouver on Saturday.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
